title: The Resurrection Commission — Matthew 28:19
paragraphs: The Resurrection Commission — Matthew 28:19
He rose.
And He did not rise so the Church could stay comfortable.
“Go therefore and make disciples of all nations…” — Matthew 28:19

That is not a soft suggestion.
That is the thunder after the empty tomb.

Jesus stepped out of death, and the first thing He gave His followers was not a seat.
It was a mission.

Not hide.
Go.

Not admire.
Make disciples.

Not build your name.
Carry His.

The Resurrection Commission means this: the risen Christ has all authority, and He sends broken people with holy purpose. The cross paid for our sin. The tomb proved His victory. And now the King sends His redeemed ones into a dying world with the only message that can raise dead hearts to life.
But here’s what we miss.

Matthew 28:19 is not just about traveling far.
It is about obeying deep.

Some people want the power of resurrection without the burden of surrender. Some want Easter joy without kingdom responsibility. But the same Jesus who conquered the grave also commands our feet, our mouth, our witness, our life.

This commission is for the timid.
For the restored.
For the once-ashamed Peter kind of people.

Because the Gospel was never for display only.
It was always for delivery.

Go to the nations.
Go to your house.
Go to your street.
Go to the one person everyone else has given up on.
Carry the name of Jesus there.

Because resurrection is not the end of the story.
It is the launch of the mission.

And the beauty of it?
He never sends us alone.

The risen Christ commands, and the risen Christ stays.
That is the fire of the Great Commission: His authority, His Gospel, His presence.

So do not just celebrate the empty tomb.
Obey the King who walked out of it.

Repent. Believe. Go.
Jesus is alive, and because He lives, the world must hear.
